articles.title: Nayara Malnero, sexóloga: "Los hombres no siempre tienen ganas"
articles.standfirst: La psicóloga y terapeuta de parejas desmonta el mito del deseo masculino permanente, advierte de que el estrés "mata el deseo" y califica el porno de "destructor de la respuesta sexual"
articles.summary: La psicóloga y terapeuta de parejas desmonta el mito del deseo masculino permanente, advierte de que el estrés "mata el deseo" y califica el porno de "destructor de la respuesta sexual"
articles.body: ¿A los hombres siempre les apetece? Nayara Malnero, sexóloga, psicóloga y terapeuta de parejas, que además está escribiendo un libro sobre sexo dirigido a hombres, lo tiene claro: no, y creer lo contrario está detrás de muchos problemas. En esta conversación para MARCA Bienestar repasa las falsas creencias sobre el deseo, las erecciones y el rendimiento. Para Malnero, el primer mito que hay que derribar es el de la disponibilidad permanente: "Creo que es hora de que nos demos cuenta de que los hombres son tan humanos como las mujeres y que, por supuesto, no siempre tienen ganas. Su deseo fluctúa igual que fluctúa el nuestro y eso no es problemático, lo problemático es pensar que siempre tienen que estar disponibles y tener ganas". Esa presión, explica, genera problemas de bajo deseo, anorgasmia, eyaculación retardada o disfunción eréctil. Tener menos deseo no significa que algo vaya mal. Significa, según la sexóloga, que "tenemos una mala educación sexual y creemos que siempre tenemos que tener el deseo muy alto, independientemente de que nuestro día haya sido horrible, que estemos mal en el trabajo, que discutamos con nuestra pareja o que tengamos problemas familiares o económicos". A eso se suman factores físicos como el sedentarismo, la mala alimentación o el mal descanso, porque "le afecta absolutamente todo el contexto del hombre: tanto físico, como mental y relacional". El estrés, explica Malnero, eleva el cortisol, que inhibe la producción de hormonas sexuales, entre ellas la testosterona, y además tensa los tejidos y dificulta los procesos sexuales. Su conclusión es rotunda: "El estrés mata el deseo y toda la función sexual. Realmente, es uno de los principales enemigos del sexo". La edad pesa menos de lo que se cree: "La edad no es un criterio tan relevante". Hay hombres muy mayores con "un rendimiento sexual y un deseo espectaculares" y jóvenes con muchas dificultades. Influye cómo se lleve: "nuestro estado de salud o nuestros hábitos en el día a día, pero no el número de años que tengamos". Sobre los 40 es igual de clara: "Realmente nada. Es un número que hemos elegido porque nos parece simbólicamente un antes y un después, pero la realidad es que nada". Reconoce que a partir de los 40 o los 50, en hombres y en mujeres, baja la testosterona y hay cambios hormonales, pero eso "no quiere decir que deje de haber deseo, de disfrute o de buen rendimiento sexual, ni para nosotras ni para ellos". La rutina de pareja, en cambio, sí afecta: "El deseo consiste en obtener aquello que no tenemos, y la rutina de pareja hace que ya lo tengamos a mano, que siempre sea igual, aburrido, y eso no es estimulante". De ahí que insista en cuidar la relación y mantener la chispa y la diversión. "No, son dos procesos fisiológicos independientes que no tienen nada que ver", responde. De hecho, apunta, "normalmente el problema está cuando hay deseo, pero la erección no responde". También puede haber erección sin connotación sexual, como ocurre con las matutinas o las espontáneas. Si aparece una disfunción, recomienda acudir a un terapeuta sexual: "Ahí estamos para echar un cable". La presión por cumplir es, según la sexóloga, una de las causas principales: "Es uno de los elementos principales por los que aparecen los problemas de erección". Señala el estrés y la ansiedad de querer rendir, de tener que tener siempre ganas y una erección potente y "ser, como se suele decir, un empotrador". El resultado es el contrario al buscado: "La erección funciona cuando el hombre está relajado y, con toda esta presión, es imposible". La buena noticia, añade, es que tiene solución, siempre que se deje de buscar donde no toca: "generalmente, es en el plano físico y las falsas creencias". Malnero es tajante: "El porno es un destructor de la respuesta sexual, tanto en hombres como en mujeres, pero, especialmente en hombres, que son los que más lo consumen habitualmente". Su razonamiento es que sobreestimula de forma muy intensa y "no tiene absolutamente nada que ver con la vida real". Si uno aprende a excitarse así a solas, en compañía aparecen la ansiedad y el estrés y el cuerpo no reacciona igual. Según ella, "hay una relación directa entre consumo habitual de pornografía y bajada del deseo sexual y disfunción eréctil". ¿Cuándo consultar? No por una mala semana. La señal es que la situación preocupe y se alargue: "Cuando nos tenga preocupados, cuando nos genere problemas de pareja, cuando sintamos de verdad que hay algo en nuestra vida que falta y que nos genera insatisfacción". Tiene que ser algo "que ocurra durante una temporada larga y que, de verdad, nos genere una preocupación a largo plazo, o un conflicto personal o de pareja".

articles.title: Newcastle care leaver finds dream job after jungle trek
articles.summary: Milly said her jungle expedition boosted her confidence and she did not miss her mobile phone.
articles.body:
A care leaver is starting a new job after returning from the trip of a lifetime.

After a traumatic childhood, Milly was moved to a children's home in Newcastle during her secondary school years, where she gained confidence to apply for, and win a place, on a 10-week adventure in Borneo.

She said she had learned "not to be afraid to speak" during her trip, which also involved building roads.

Milly has now found employment with a building firm.

During her Raleigh International expedition in Malaysia, she also spent time working in a wildlife sanctuary, as well as trekking in the jungle.

"We were walking like for hours, in the middle of nowhere, with people I'd just met.

"That's when I hit breaking point. I just wanted to go home," she said.

Milly said it had felt rewarding to make it to the end and the confidence-boosting experience would live with her forever.

She said she had learned "how to speak to people, and not to hide myself. And not to be afraid to speak. Now I just don't shut up."

Milly said she had thought the hardest part of the trip would be not having her mobile phone.

"Everyone thinks it's horror that I had no phone. But I actually got to speak to people and really have a conversation," she said.

Milly has now found employment with building firm Robertsons.

She is training in various construction industry roles, on the site of the new Sir Bobby Robson Institute at the Freeman Hospital.

"I very much surprised myself. I didn't think I'd get a job like this when I left the children's home," she said.

Neil Kennedy, the North East managing director of Robertson Construction, said he had been wowed by the 19-year-old and her positive attitude.

"Milly has got something about her. I guess she's got resilience. She is a young female in a male-dominated industry, but Milly handles herself exemplary," he said.

Milly said she now hoped to secure an apprenticeship with the firm and follow her dream of becoming a joiner.

She said she was thankful someone had seen her potential.

"It just feels nice that someone thought, 'I'm going to give her a chance.' I've took it with both hands, and I'm doing the best I can."

articles.title: 1 missing, 4 rushed to hospital after helicopter crashes off Southern California island
articles.summary: A medevac helicopter crashed off Catalina Island in California with five aboard, leaving one person missing as search and rescue operations continue.
articles.body: A medevac helicopter crashed into the water off Catalina Island in California on Wednesday night, with one of the five people aboard reported missing and the other four taken to hospitals, according to officials. The Los Angeles County Fire Department received reports of the crash shortly before 8 p.m. Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with the fire department dispatching helicopters and divers shortly after learning of the crash. 3 DEAD, 1 HOSPITALIZED AFTER NEWS HELICOPTER CRASHES IN LOS ANGELES COMMERCIAL AREA The U.S. Coast Guard also responded to the crash. "I have been informed that a medevac helicopter leaving Catalina Island has crashed shortly after takeoff. L.A. County Fire, Sheriff, Coast Guard, and Avalon Fire are on the scene," Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn said on X. "Search and rescue operations are underway, and I am praying for everyone who was on board." At least one of the five people aboard the helicopter remains unaccounted for as of late Wednesday night. Two others were transported to hospitals in stable condition and the remaining two were transported in unknown condition, according to KTLA. The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said two people were taken to a hospital on Catalina Island, while two others were transported to the Ronald Reagan Medical Center at UCLA. The fire department said the helicopter's flight plan was unclear, according to CBS LA. Deputies said the helicopter belonged to Reach Air Medical Services. articles.title: Surprising culprit tied to 1 in 8 cancer cases worldwide, major study reveals
articles.summary: A new IARC analysis links 2.3 million cancer cases worldwide to 12 infections, with H. pylori, HPV and hepatitis B leading the global burden.
articles.body: About one in eight new cancer cases worldwide in 2024 — 2.3 million cases — have been linked to infections, according to a new analysis from the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC). The researchers identified 12 specific infections that were linked to human cancer cases, including Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus, Schistosoma haematobium, HTLV-1, Opisthorchis viverrini, Clonorchis sinensis, Merkel cell polyomavirus and HIV. The following five infections contributed to nearly all the global cases. POPULAR DAILY DRINKING HABIT COULD NEARLY TRIPLE RISK OF DEADLY CANCER, MAJOR STUDY FINDS "The findings underscore the major role that infection control can play in reducing the global cancer burden," said study co-author Dr. Harriet Rumgay, a scientist in the Cancer Surveillance Branch at IARC, in a press release. "Despite progress in vaccination and screening, infection-related cancers remain a major global challenge, with the burden falling disproportionately on populations in low- and middle-income countries." CANCER DOCTOR REVEALS 5 HABITS THAT MAY REDUCE DISEASE RISK AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES The researchers say many of these cancers could have been prevented through vaccination, treatment or screenings. The study, conducted in France, analyzed cancer data from 2024. The findings were published in The Lancet Oncology on Sept. 28. Study limitations The study had several limitations, the researchers acknowledged. Because the study used population-level estimates rather than tracking individual patients over time, the results depended on the quality of available cancer data in each country. Additionally, it only included infections already proven to cause cancer, so the total impact could be underestimated. "We know that there are certain infections that we are exposed to over our lifetime that may result in an increased risk of certain cancers," Dr. Joshua Cohen, medical director of the Gynecologic Cancer Program of City of Hope Orange County in Irvine, California, told Fox News Digital. "However, most cancers are not caused by infection." DOCTORS PUSH NEW BLOOD TESTS FOR COLON CANCER AS CASES SURGE IN YOUNGER ADULTS HPV is one of the most common drivers of cancers that arise along the rectum, vagina or cervix, as well as the oropharynx (back of the throat), according to Cohen, who was not involved in the study. "Eighty percent of the population has been exposed to certain types of HPV strains," he said. "About 40,000 people in the U.S. are diagnosed with these cancers each year." "Most cancers are not caused by infection." For most people who are exposed to HPV, the body will clear the virus on its own, Cohen said. "We don't know why some patients' immune systems allow them to clear the HPV infection and some don't." Another very common cancer, although less so in the U.S., is gastric cancer, he noted, which is linked to H. Pylori, an infection in the stomach. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "We don't screen everybody for H. pylori in the U.S. — it's more common in other parts of the world, like Southeast Asia." However, those who have peptic ulcer disease or significant epigastric pain should talk with a gastroenterologist about getting screened and treated for H. pylori, the doctor advised. Prevention strategies There are things people can do to reduce the risk of infection-related cancers, according to Cohen. "As a patient, the most important thing is to think about your health, what you can do to prevent yourself from developing these infections or your family," he said. "And if you do have one of these infections, what can you do to reduce your risk of developing a subsequent cancer?" Cohen emphasized that Americans have access to an HPV vaccination that can help prevent many of these infections. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "If you’re under the age of 45 and you've not had an HPV vaccination, there is various good safety data that you should get vaccinated," he said. "That will cover, at least in the U.S., most risks regarding oropharyngeal cancers, vaginal cancers, cervical cancers, penile cancers and anal cancers." The doctor reiterated that developing one of the listed infections doesn’t necessarily mean someone will develop cancer. "The vast majority of patients who have an HPV infection or H. Pylori, or even hepatitis B or C, are not going to develop cancer," he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER But because these infections have been associated with certain cancers, it’s important to seek treatment for them. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Symptoms such as epigastric pain (pain or discomfort in the upper middle part of your abdomen), acid reflux, abnormal vaginal bleeding or pain with swallowing could be related to medical conditions that may be associated with certain infections or cancer, the doctor warned. "There are steps we can take as doctors to keep you safe and hopefully reduce the risk of developing cancer for those that have had an infection," Cohen added.

articles.title: Here’s How Many Whole Grains To Eat in a Day To Boost Heart Health
articles.summary: Whole grains are linked to better heart health, and a study found four-to-six daily servings lower the risk of heart disease. How to boost whole grain intake.
articles.body: Whole grains have long been linked to better heart health, but researchers have now found the sweet spot for how many daily servings lower the risk of heart disease. Meeting the recommendations can be as easy as snacking on popcorn — hold the salt and butter — and making sure your sandwich bread is full of whole grains. Whole grain cereal, the healthiest type cereal, can also be an important part of the routine. Heart Health Tip of the Day: Eat At Least 4 Servings of Whole Grains Every Day A diet rich in whole-grain foods, defined as four to six servings a day, likely prevents heart disease by lowering body weight, blood pressure, waist circumference, triglycerides and LDL cholesterol — the kind that clogs arteries, a meta-analysis of randomized trials found. The results were recently published in the European Heart Journal. “Increasing whole grain intake is a relatively simple, accessible and affordable dietary strategy that can complement other lifestyle and medical interventions,” said lead author, Dr. Helda Tutunchi, an associate professor of nutritional sciences at Iran’s Tabriz University of Medical Sciences, in a statement. “One important finding is that whole grains may benefit cardiovascular health through several modest improvements acting together, rather than through one large effect on a single risk factor. We observed improvements across multiple pathways, including blood lipids, blood pressure, glucose regulation, body fat and some markers of inflammation.” Improving several risk factors all at once could mean a greater reduction in cardiovascular risk over the long-term, she added. Why It Matters A whole grain contains all three parts of the grain seed: the bran, germ and endosperm, according to the Whole Grains Council. Grains that can be consumed in this complete form include wheat, rice, oats, quinoa, corn and many more. But choosing white rice or white bread, for example, means you’re missing at least one part of the grain. While the underlying mechanisms for how whole grains lower cardiovascular disease risk factors so effectively “remain unclear,” according to the study, they come with key health benefits. All three parts of the grain house important nutrients, including antioxidants, protein, B vitamins, and fiber, said registered dietitian Natalie Rizzo, nutrition editor for TODAY. Fiber helps regulate blood sugar by slowing down the rate of glucose in the bloodstream, and it promotes satiety, which helps with weight management, dietitians previously told TODAY.com. Soluble fiber, the type that dissolves in water, traps cholesterol before it enters the bloodstream so that it’s excreted in a bowel movement. How to Get Started Aim to eat at least one serving of whole grains at every meal and incorporate them into snacks as well. A serving can be a bowl of oatmeal, a sandwich made with whole grain bread or a helping of brown rice. Choose whole grain cereal for breakfast and make healthy fruit-and-nut cookies to satisfy a sweet craving. Snack on popcorn, which is a whole grain. Just make sure it’s air-popped, stick to extra virgin olive oil as the topping and add only a dash of salt. “Popcorn is healthiest when it doesn’t contain any additives. When you start adding butter, salt or other toppings, it becomes less healthy,” Rizzo said. articles.title: Odisha study finds high depression risk in eye patients with chronic illnesses
articles.summary: Odisha study: 1 in 6 eye clinic patients show depression; risk rises with multiple chronic illnesses like hypertension and diabetes, urging routine mental health screening.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Eye patients suffering from multiple chronic illnesses are significantly more likely to experience depression, highlighting need for routine mental health screening in ophthalmology clinics, according to a new study conducted in Odisha.The research found that nearly one in six patients attending an eye clinic showed signs of depression, while the burden increased sharply among those living with additional chronic diseases.The study, titled ‘Prevalence of anxiety and depression among multimorbid patients attending eye clinics in Odisha, India: A hospital-based study’, was published in the journal Clinical Epidemiology and Global Health.Seven researchers from ICMR-National Institute of Health Research, Bhubaneswar, and KIMS Hospital here surveyed 404 adults attending a tertiary eye-care hospital in Bhubaneswar to examine prevalence of anxiety and depression among patients with eye ailments and other chronic conditions.The study found hypertension to be the most common coexisting illness among eye patients, affecting 67.25% of participants, followed by diabetes at 37.06%. The most prevalent disease combination was hypertension along with an eye condition, seen in 31.19% of patients. Another 22.52% had both diabetes and hypertension in addition to their eye disorder.Researchers reported that 17.57% of participants had signs of depression, while anxiety was found in 1.73%. However, a much larger proportion of patients fell into the borderline category for depression, suggesting a substantial hidden burden of psychological distress among people undergoing treatment for eye diseases.G Nageswar Rao and others in the research paper said the prevalence of depression increased with the number of chronic illnesses. Among patients with an eye condition and three or more additional diseases, only 11.63% were classified as normal for depression, while 46.51% showed borderline symptoms and 41.86% had abnormal depression scores, they added.Researchers noted a statistically significant association between multimorbidity and depression.ICMR-NIHR director Sanghamitra Pati said visual impairment, fear of vision loss, dependence on caregivers, repeated hospital visits and limitations in daily activities can contribute to emotional distress. Combination of eye diseases with conditions such as hypertension and diabetes may further worsen mental well-being, she added.“The findings underline need to integrate mental health assessment into eye-care services,” said Pati.They recommended routine screening for anxiety and depression among patients with eye-related multimorbidity and closer collaboration between ophthalmologists, primary care physicians and mental health professionals.Early identification and treatment of psychological distress could improve adherence to treatment, follow-up care and overall quality of life, the study noted.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.title: Suvendu promises model status, hospital, college in Rejinagar
articles.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari promises to make Rejinagar a model constituency with a 200-bed hospital, college, bridge, industries and jobs.
articles.body: Rejinagar/Kolkata: CM Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday promised to turn Rejinagar into a “model assembly constituency”, pledging a 200-bed hospital, a college, a bridge, new industries and five milk collection centres over the next one-and-a-half years. He also said he would open a public service centre in the name of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, similar to initiatives he said he had undertaken in Bhowanipore and Nandigram.“My Hindu brothers will say ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and my minority brothers will say ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’,” Adhikari said.He said he had spent around two hours travelling through Rejinagar and interacting with residents as part of his public outreach. He also visited the memorial of Mir Madan, commander of the Nawab of Bengal’s forces at the Battle of Plassey, and the home of six-year-old Jasmina Khatun, who died on Tuesday after suffering critical injuries while trying to collect lozenges thrown from an election campaign vehicle during a Democratic Trinamool Congress roadshow. Adhikari promised assistance to the girl’s family after the election.“From village after village, minorities who had not voted for the BJP till now are standing in queues, shaking hands with the CM and saying that they will not waste their votes,” Adhikari said.Referring to an incident at the railway ground in Shaktipur in 2019, Adhikari alleged TMC workers and a section of the administration had removed microphones and loudspeakers to prevent BJP from holding a meeting. He said those who had opposed him in the past were now welcoming him. “I have not forgotten. Everything will be accounted for,” he said.“Those who show arrogance, insolence and pride, and those who wish for people’s death, their downfall is inevitable; no one will be able to stop it,” he said, criticising Humayun Kabir over his remarks wishing death upon the Bengal CM, citing incidents involving Ajit Pawar, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi.Adhikari also made a series of promises on industrialisation, employment and financial assistance. He said 40,000 migrant workers would be brought back from outside the state within two years. He promised 125 days of work over the next six months at Rs 300 a day, amounting to Rs 37,500, and an additional Rs 3,000 under the PM-Kisan Yojana.He said industrial activity would begin taking shape in Rejinagar within the next one-and-a-half years, with the aim of creating unskilled jobs for migrant workers who had moved to states such as Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.“Within the next one-and-a-half years, you will see smoke rising from factories in the Rejinagar industrial belt. articles.title: Amanda Peet Reveals First ‘Weird’ Sign of Breast Cancer. It Wasn’t a Lump
articles.summary: Amanda Peet had an early breast cancer warning sign six months before she was diagnosed. She reveals the skin symptom that she calls “weird.” It wasn’t a lump.
articles.body: Amanda Peet was diagnosed with breast cancer last fall, but she had an early warning sign that something was wrong six months earlier. The actor revealed the “weird” symptom during an interview with TODAY on Thursday, Oct. 1. “I was in my closet, I was probably putting something on and I felt a weird — it just didn’t feel like normal skin, but it wasn’t the frozen pea that everybody talks about,” Peet, 54, told Savannah Guthrie, referring to what a breast cancer lump can feel like. “I went and I even got an MRI and then they sent me away. So I thought I had a clean bill of health, but they were actually watching it.” Six months later, on the Friday before Labor Day in 2025, the actor thought she was going in for a routine scan, when her doctor spotted something concerning on her ultrasound, Peet wrote in an essay for The New Yorker. She knew something was wrong because her physician, who was usually very chatty, went silent. The doctor then performed a biopsy and told her she would walk the sample over to Cedars-Sinai and hand-deliver it on a Friday night, another concerning clue. Peet said she’ll never forget the moment when she received her breast cancer diagnosis in a call soon after. While lumps are the most common breast cancer symptom, skin changes like dents, swelling and redness can also be a warning sign. Skin that appears pitted, like the skin of an orange, is among breast cancer symptom a doctor monitors in herself. Once diagnosed, Peet recalled having to deal with a “slow drip of information” about the treatment options, genetic information and hormone receptor status. “If you’re an anxious person, it’s your basic nightmare,” she noted. The actor was diagnosed with hormone-receptor-positive and HER2-negative lobular breast cancer and underwent a lumpectomy and radiation. Lobular breast cancer accounts for 15% of all new breast cancer diagnoses, according to the National Cancer Institute. Tumors don’t usually form in lumps, making them hard to detect, especially in women with dense breast tissue, it notes. Peet has dense breasts and was told she needed extra monitoring. She’d been seeing a breast surgeon every six months for checkups, she wrote in her essay. Her cancer was caught early, at Stage 1. “I think about how lucky I was in so many ways,” she said. Peet previously told Hoda Kotb that she has great health insurance, lots of support from her friends and family and a nanny. “There were a lot of people around to take care of me, but not everybody has that,” she said. “So I’ve also been giving that a lot of thought.”

articles.standfirst: No es una consecuencia normal de la ingesta de alcohol
articles.summary: No es una consecuencia normal de la ingesta de alcohol
articles.body: El consumo de alcohol cada vez se reduce más y más. Sin embargo, muchos siguen considerando que esta sustancia tan nociva es la mejor acompañante de comidas, fiestas, celebraciones y ocio en general. Muchas personas aún consumen excesiva cantidad de alcohol, notando sus consecuencias más inmediatas al día siguiente. Una de esas consecuencias es la diarrea. Así lo menciona Saúl Sánchez, nutricionista, quien califica que esta consecuencia no es lógica, sino que puede significar un problema real interno en tu organismo. El experto menciona un estudio en el que se muestra que, el riesgo de cáncer de colon es el doble en aquellas personas que responden al consumo de alcohol con un síntoma como el de la diarrea. El efecto viene provocado por una mutación genética que hace que, el tóxico, permanezca más tiempo en el organismo, afectando así y de esta manera a la microbiota y al intestino. Para los bebedores de alcohol ocasionales se multiplica el riesgo de cáncer de colón por dos pero, para los bebedores habituales el riesgo asciende a cuatro veces más. El especialista menciona que, el consumo de alcohol, no es recomendable para nadie, para ningún individuo. Sin embargo, si presentas este síntoma, la diarrea, después de haber bebido alcohol (ya sea en las horas posteriores o al día siguiente), deberías evitarlo por completo. Una de las principales cosas que debes hacer es evitar la compra de la sustancia. Para ello, evita tener botellas en casa para no caer en la tentación. También es recomendable que te alejes de los desencadenantes sorteando aquellos lugares, fiestas o amistades que te presionen o te inciten a beber. Por otro lado, es necesario aprender a decir que no cuando te ofrecen y saber qué bebidas pueden sustituir aquellas alcohólicas, además de alternar con agua para que así no consumas tanto alcohol. Además, consumir comida antes y durante el consumo de alcohol, ya que nunca debes beber con el estómago vacío, puesto que los alimentos ayudan a disminuir la absorción de esta sustancia. Además, siempre que quieras consumir pequeñas cantidades de alcohol, procura que sea en recipientes pequeños, en cantidades moderadas en vasos o copas de tamaño más pequeño para controlar de una mejor manera la cantidad que estás consumiendo. Sea el motivo que sea por el que quieres dejar de consumir esta sustancia, la realidad es que lo más recomendable abandonar este hábito por completo o reducirlo a lo mínimo posible.

articles.title: Kennedy to roll out $10 million challenge to encourage Presidential Fitness Test in schools
articles.summary: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. plans to announce a nationwide competition for schools aimed at expanding participation in the Presidential Fitness Test.
articles.body: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. plans to announce a new nationwide competition for schools aimed at expanding participation in the Presidential Fitness Test, which President Donald Trump revived last year. The challenge will offer $7 million in prizes to schools, districts and youth organizations that demonstrate effective ways to implement the test, the Health and Human Services Department told NBC News. Another $3 million in awards and vouchers will be available for fitness or sports equipment. Trump signed an executive order last year to bring the test back to schools. But only 161 schools on U.S. military installations are required to do so, so the administration has looked for ways to boost participation. Starting Thursday, organizations can apply for the cash prizes on a new federal website, Fitness.gov. Entries can be submitted until February, then winners are expected to be announced in the spring. The fitness test is a lengthy tradition in public elementary, middle and high schools that measures children’s physical health based on their performance in various cardiovascular and strength exercises. Children compete to win awards by hitting certain benchmarks for their age and sex, such as running a mile in under 10 minutes. The exercises for the revived test under the Trump administration include a one-mile run, curl-ups, planks, pushups, pullups and shuttle runs. The test aligns with a broader interest in fitness among several top Trump administration officials. Kennedy, who often shares his own workout videos on social media, has pledged to reverse what he describes as an “epidemic” of chronic disease in children in part by lowering obesity rates through exercise. And Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has tightened fitness standards for military troops. The Defense Department posted a video last year of Kennedy and Hegseth challenging each other to a pushup and pullup competition. Trump has also promised “a golden age for American sports” as the 2028 Summer Olympics approach. A variation of the same Presidential Fitness Test was implemented in public schools from 1956 until the 2012-13 school year, when the Obama administration replaced it with the Presidential Youth Fitness Program, which focused on individual health and aimed to minimize comparisons between children. Kennedy has criticized that change, arguing that competition is good for children. “If we’re going to be competitive internationally, we need to be competitive with each other. We need to teach people how to win and how to lose and how to process victory and defeat,” he said at the signing of Trump’s executive order last year. Kennedy’s uncle John F. Kennedy made a similar argument shortly after he was elected president in 1960. Kennedy has often pointed to the era of his uncle’s presidency as a time when American children were healthier, but the reality is complicated. While kids were less sedentary in the 1960s, their life expectancy is higher today, and while rates of some chronic diseases are rising among children, the trend is sometimes attributable to improvements in screening and detection. Increases in childhood obesity and Type 2 diabetes, however, are strongly associated with diets heavy in processed food and sedentary lifestyles. Experts widely agree that young people should be more active. The federal government recommends that children ages 6 to 17 get at least an hour of moderate or vigorous physical activity each day. Only 20% to 28% of kids meet that goal, according to the Physical Activity Alliance, an advocacy group that promotes physical fitness. However, some researchers who study physical activity among children worry that dividing kids into winners and losers the way the Presidential Fitness Test does could discourage them from engaging in fitness. The test also rewards certain types of athletic ability, they say, when there are other ways to be physically active. Russell Pate, a professor of exercise science at the University of South Carolina, said the test is not an indicator of overall health. Many schools already use a program called FitnessGram to holistically assess a child’s physical health rather than their athletic skills, he said. Most kids will also find it difficult to meet the benchmarks for the Presidential Fitness Award, he added. “It’s based on high-level performance in all the test items, and we know from long, hard experience that only a very small percentage of kids realistically can achieve that,” he said.

articles.title: Woman With Breast Cancer at 26 Had to Pay $20,000 Out of Pocket for Care Due to Insurance Issues
articles.summary: Iris Di Cesare speaks to TODAY.com about receiving her breast cancer diagnosis and the financial burden it became when she unexpectedly lost her real estate job.
articles.body: Iris Di Cesare noticed her first breast lump in 2016, when she was a college senior. “I had an ultrasound, a biopsy, and it was benign,” she recalls to TODAY.com. Her doctor explained that it was a fibroadenoma, a marble-sized noncancerous breast tumor, and that she should “keep an eye on it,” so she did. Several years later, in February 2022, she discovered an even larger lump, but she brushed it off. “I thought maybe it was because of my period or because, you know, I’m just going crazy,” she explains. By April, however, it was undeniable. “It had drastically gotten bigger,” she says. Breast Cancer at 26 Di Cesare, who lives in Chicago, went to her gynecologist to have the lump inspected, and a week later, she was getting an ultrasound at Northwestern University’s Department of Medicine. Soon after, she got the mammogram, and the day after that, the lump was biopsied. Although she hadn’t noticed it at first, the skin around her nipple had also started to change. What was once smooth had rippled, creating an uneven texture she’d never had before. A quick internet search indicated it could be a cancer symptom. She willed herself to stay calm. She’d been in this position before, had these thoughts before, and everything had turned out fine. If it wasn’t cancer, she could deal with it, Di Cesare remembers thinking to herself. She wasn’t sure she could deal with the alternative. But she was going to have to. The biopsy confirmed her second breast tumor was cancerous, nestled next to the benign one. “Had I never had my benign one, I never would have known my baseline — what felt normal. I never would have been vigilant about keeping an eye on that area,” says Di Cesare. At 26 years old, she was diagnosed with Stage 3 invasive, hormone-positive, ductal carcinoma, a type of breast cancer. Still, the Northwestern doctor who delivered the news reassured her that it was “the most common, the most treatable, and I felt better knowing that,” Di Cesare says. Immediate Treatment Di Cesare’s treatment plan was initiated quickly. “They got me in really fast,” she says. That May, she began three months of chemotherapy every other week. Then she took August to rest before having surgery in September 2022. Although the cancer was in her right breast, Di Cesare elected to have a nipple-sparing double mastectomy, where both breasts were removed. She knew that the data shows removing both breasts doesn’t improve survival rates in most women who have cancer in only one breast. And because she didn’t have a family history of breast cancer, there was no recommendation to do so by her doctor. But she wanted peace of mind. “I want to do everything I can to not have to do this journey of cancer ever again,” she says. During the operation, Di Cesare’s doctors also removed 20 lymph nodes and determined the cancer had spread to two of them. Next came 25 days of daily radiation therapy and four breast reconstruction surgeries by a plastic surgeon. Side Effects Paired With Financial Challenges Most of Di Cesare’s physical side effects are overshadowed by fatigue. “That’s probably my biggest one,” she says. “There’s no describing the fatigue. It’s just there.” The medication she’s required to take for the next few years brings it on. She’s also in medically induced menopause which means hot flashes, insomnia and sexual changes. Di Cesare’s cancer journey could have ended there — fatigue among other side effects and a rotation of drugs to keep her healthy — but she had to fight financially, too. When she was diagnosed, Di Cesare had just switched to her own insurance plan, like many 26-year-olds. “Navigating insurance (from) a normal standpoint can be confusing,” she says. “Let alone now you’re going to the doctor constantly. Now you have to meet your deductible and co-pays, and it’s, like, I don’t even know what this means.” Di Cesare was spending thousands of dollars on her medical care because she had no other choice. And then, after radiation, and once she’d begun her drug cocktail, she lost her job. “The company I worked for went under,” she says. She and other former employees were told they’d have insurance for a while longer, but her coverage ended sooner than she was told it would, which would have resulted in a gap in her coverage. Di Cesare couldn’t have that. So, she turned to the place she was spending a great deal of time anyway: the hospital. The social workers at Northwestern “were able to help me find state insurance,” she says. And they connected her with the Illinois Breast and Cervical Cancer Program, which offers free testing and exams to eligible women. Di Cesare calls it a lifesaver. “That covered all of my medicine and all of my treatment and all of my doctor appointments. So that was a blessing that I needed,” she adds. “Many (cancer patients) draw from savings, including retirement accounts, take on debt through credit cards or loans, or make difficult decisions about household spending,” Shane Jacobson, chief executive officer at the American Cancer Society (ACS) and the American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network (ACS CAN), tells TODAY.com. “Some delay filling prescriptions, postpone follow-up appointments or skip recommended care because of cost,” he adds. And that’s only about the medical side of things. Transportation, lodging and childcare all add up, too. Even with comprehensive insurance, he says, patients might spend tens of thousands on their care out-of-pocket. “Average annual costs exceeded $6,000 for patients with breast, colorectal, and lung cancers,” he adds. Nearly half of cancer patients have medical debt, and nearly all of them have insurance. A single diagnosis is more than illness and subsequent treatment, Di Cesare quickly learned. It’s both “cancer and financial toxicity,” says Jacobson. “For those unable to work, programs such as Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) can provide support,” he adds. “Medicaid, Medicare, Marketplace coverage, and other public assistance programs may also help families navigate coverage gaps and financial hardship.” Di Cesare shares her story to raise awareness of breast cancer symptoms and the resources available to help pay for care. She urges women to know their baseline, as she did. Don’t wait for the lump. Be familiar with your breasts, check your clavicle area, she says, and feel your armpits. Know what’s normal so you know when to seek medical attention. It made all the difference for Di Cesare. And while “it was a journey,” she says, “it’s positive now. So, (I’m) thankful for that.”

articles.title: Ambulance stopped for CM Himanta’s convoy: 4 Assam cops suspended
articles.summary: Four Assam police officers were suspended after stopping an ambulance for CM Himanta Biswa Sarma’s convoy in Silchar; the cirrhosis patient died a day later.
articles.body: SILCHAR: Four cops managing traffic in south Assam’s Silchar were suspended Thursday for briefly stopping an ambulance ferrying a critically ill patient the previous day to let CM Himanta Biswa Sarma’s convoy pass.The action, coinciding with the 47-year-old cirrhosis patient’s death at Silchar Medical College and Hospital, came a day after Himanta ordered an inquiry and publicly apologised to the family for what he termed an “unacceptable” violation of his standing order not to inconvenience ordinary citizens in the name of VIP movement.The ambulance taking deceased Rasaraj Chakraborty to hospital had to stop for about four minutes near Ramnagar ISBT as police cleared the route for Sarma’s convoy. The CM came to know about it after a video purportedly showing the ambulance waiting for his convoy to pass did the rounds of social media platforms.“Emergency medical care must take precedence over VIP movement,” Sarma said. “Under no circumstances should the movement of ambulances or other emergency vehicles be impeded on account of VIP convoy arrangements.”He warned that guidelines governing convoy movement must be implemented “in letter and spirit”.While condoling Chakraborty’s death a day later, the CM said the unfortunate culmination of his disease and the ambulance being stopped on the way to hospital were unconnected. “The patient was suffering from a critical liver ailment and his death is not related to the brief halt,” he told reporters in Nagaon.He iterated anyone in the CM’s chair was “merely a chief servant” and “new Assam has no place for VIP culture”.Chakraborty’s wife said the family had lost its breadwinner and appealed to Sarma for assistance. “He has left behind two children. articles.title: What to know about pentobarbital after death row inmate survives 2 lethal injection doses
articles.summary: A look at pentobarbital reveals why the barbiturate used in Christa Gail Pike's failed lethal injection may not have reached fatal concentrations.
articles.body: A high-profile execution attempt in Nashville ended in chaos and raised urgent medical questions after Tennessee death row inmate Christa Gail Pike survived two separate doses of lethal pentobarbital, the Associated Press reported. Pentobarbital is a short-acting barbiturate, according to medical authorities at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Historically prescribed as a sedative, anti-seizure medication or sleep aid, pentobarbital enhances the activity of GABA, the brain's primary inhibitory neurotransmitter, slowing activity throughout the central nervous system. TENNESSEE DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES IN FAILED EXECUTION ATTEMPT In clinical medicine, pentobarbital has been used for several purposes, including: Because newer, safer drugs with lower risks of overdose have largely replaced barbiturates in hospital settings, pentobarbital is now rarely used in routine patient care. However, it remains a primary agent in veterinary euthanasia and lethal injection protocols across several U.S. states, according to the National Library of Medicine, FDA-approved veterinary drug labeling and the Death Penalty Information Center. How pentobarbital is used in lethal injections In a high-dose lethal injection protocol, pentobarbital is administered intravenously in large, ultra-lethal quantities — typically 2.5 to 5 grams (far exceeding clinical therapeutic doses). JUDGE BLOCKS ALABAMA'S NITROGEN GAS EXECUTION METHOD, RULES IT IS UNCONSTITUTIONALLY CRUEL When injected directly into a vein, the progression follows three stages, according to medical sources. What happened in the Christa Pike execution? Pike, 50, who was convicted in the 1995 murder of classmate Colleen Slemmer, was slated to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Media witnesses observed her asking if her arm was supposed to feel that way (burning), breathing raggedly, and audibly snoring behind closed curtains over an hour-long span. The incident prompted Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to halt all remaining executions in the state pending an independent investigation. State officials maintained that they strictly adhered to the protocol and that the chemical supply was verified. Media witnesses and defense court filings described several problems during the procedure. Several possible explanations have been raised in court filings and medical literature, although no cause has been confirmed in Pike’s case. articles.title: 8 Alandi coaching institute students on picnic drown near Diveagar beach
articles.summary: Eight 16-year-old Alandi coaching institute students drowned during a picnic at Diveagar beach in Raigad; police registered accidental death, teachers claim warnings.
articles.body: Pune/Navi Mumbai: A picnic to Diveagar beach in Raigad district turned tragic on Thursday as eight students of a private coaching institute in Alandi drowned in the sea.A total of 42 students — 25 boys and 17 girls — accompanied by six teachers from Winners Academy and Study Centre in Alandi had visited Diveagar, about 160km from Pune. Some students ventured into the sea around 3pm and eight of them drowned.Workers of a local water sports club entered the sea after the remaining students and teachers on the beach raised an alarm and recovered the bodies of all eight students by 5pm. The bodies were sent to Shrivardhan Rural Hospital for postmortem. The remaining 34 students were shifted to a hotel in Diveagar.Raigad police identified the deceased as Rajveer Vahile, Soham Bhandwalkar, Kaustubh Daund, Yash Wankhede, Kaiwalya Vasankar, Tanmay Vahile, Sumit Ahire and Pranav Bansode from Alandi. All were 16 years old.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis offered condolences to the families of the deceased students. “The incident is extremely heart-wrenching. All the students were from Alandi, and the local administration is coordinating to bring their bodies home,” Fadnavis wrote on X.Deputy chief minister and Pune’s guardian minister Sunetra Pawar said, “The drowning of eight students from Alandi is extremely tragic. I spoke to the Raigad district collector and superintendent of police, and instructed them to take all necessary actions. I share the grief of families of the students who lost their lives. I pray to God to give strength to the families to bear the loss.”Assistant police inspector Santosh Awati, in charge of Dighi Coastal police station, said the students of the private coaching institute had first visited Raigad Fort. They reached Diveagar in the afternoon.Bhau Salunke, the owner of Mahakali Water Sports Club in Diveagar, told TOI that he had approached the students around 2.30pm to ask if they wanted to go on a boat ride. “The students told me that they had planned to bathe in the sea and did not want a boat ride,” he said.Eight students entered the sea. Some of them did not know how to swim. The teachers claimed that they had told the students not to venture deep into the sea, but the eight boys went to chest-deep water and were dragged by the current. “As the boys gasped for breath, the teachers and other students shouted for help,” assistant police inspector Awati said.Salunke said he learnt about the tragedy while returning home and ran back to the beach. “I saw the girls in the group crying. They told me that one of their fellow students had drowned. I immediately alerted my workers and entered the sea with two jet skis around 3.30pm,” he said.Awati said a police team reached the beach after receiving information about the accident. The eight boys were unconscious after apparently gulping down seawater while drowning.“The police attempted to give CPR to the boys, but they did not regain consciousness. They were rushed to the hospital, where they were declared brought dead. An accidental death case has been registered,” assistant police inspector Awati said.The academy said it had obtained consent forms from all enrolled students before the picnic. The deceased students were from its Std XI and XII science batches. The academy issued a statement informing parents about the tragedy and told the parents of the eight deceased students to reach Shrivardhan Rural Hospital.Pintu Vahile, the uncle of victim Tanmay Vahile, told TOI, “Tanmay was in Std XI and brilliant in academics. He had topped his school in Std X. We are yet to get details about what exactly happened. Our relatives and friends have gone to bring his body.”Rajveer Vahile and Soham Bhandwalkar, two other victims, were residents of Kelgaon, adjacent to Alandi. Rajveer’s father is the village police patil. Soham’s father is a farmer.Prashant Kurhade, the president of Alandi Municipal Council (AMC), told TOI, “The victims are from Alandi and neighbouring villages. We are in contact with their relatives. Some parents left for the site after receiving information from the police this evening. We are trying to gather information about the trip and how the coaching class organised it. Except emergency services, all businesses will remain closed on Friday to pay condolence to the students.”Madhav Khandekar, the chief officer of AMC, said the coaching institute had been operating for the past two years. “The owner is from Kolhapur. The coaching class is not registered with us,” he said.A team of police personnel was deployed in front of the coaching institute.A section of schoolteachers and residents said private coaching institutes often organised educational or recreational trips to create a “positive impression” among students and parents. “But often these trips are not organised in accordance with govt guidelines,” a schoolteacher from Alandi said.He said parents were often left with little choice when coaching institutes made such trips mandatory. “They are left with no option but to agree,” the teacher said.14 students drowned 10 years agoFourteen computer science students, including twin sisters, drowned when they ventured into the sea off Murud beach on Feb 1, 2016.Six others were rescued by local residents. Of the 14 who died, 10 were girls and four were boys. In all, 115 BSc (computer science) students had gone on a picnic to Murud in three private buses, accompanied by eight teaching and three non-teaching staff members of Abeda Inamdar College of Arts, Science and Commerce in Pune’s Camp area.(With inputs from Anurag Bende)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: Kratom industry warns synthetic opioids should not be called 'kratom'
articles.summary: The American Kratom Association claims products found near two dead Ole Miss students were synthetic opioids, not natural kratom, amid pending toxicology.
articles.body: Amid the ongoing investigation into the deaths of two Ole Miss students, representatives of the kratom industry are speaking out about how the product may have been mischaracterized. Court documents show that Aidan Hamilton, 18, and Robert Strang, 20, were discovered dead on Sept. 21 at separate locations. Initial reports stated that products described as "packaged kratom" or "synthetic kratom" were found near both students. In a Sept. 30 statement, however, investigators said only that "packaging associated with kratom-related products" had been recovered at both locations. WHAT IS KRATOM? RISKS OF POPULAR SUBSTANCE REVEALED AFTER COLLEGE STUDENTS' DEATHS "During the investigations, packaging associated with kratom-related products was discovered at both locations," Lafayette County Metro Narcotics, a department in the sheriff's office, said in the statement Wednesday. Toxicology results from the medical examiner are still pending. Packaging found near both students bears the name Modus, according to court documents. The affidavit describes the tablets as Smax Pseudo-DHM, and lists pseudoindoxyl and MGM-15(DHM) among the ingredients on the pack found near Hamilton. Mac Haddow, senior fellow on public policy at the American Kratom Association in Virginia, spoke with Fox News Digital Thursday about the initial reports of packaged kratom at the two locations where the students were discovered. OLE MISS NAMES STUDENTS FOUND DEAD AS OFFICIAL ADDRESSES POTENTIAL FOR FOUL PLAY "We were deeply concerned with that characterization because it is highly unlikely, if not statistically improbable, that a natural kratom leaf product would be the cause of two deaths independently, let alone one," he said. After attempting to contact the Oxford Police Department, Haddow said the association held a news conference in Oxford asking for clarification on why officials would have disclosed a packaged kratom product. The clarification showed that the products recovered were "chemically manipulated opioids, not kratom," Haddow added. "We are grateful for the clarification because what they have told us and disclosed is that these, in fact, were highly synthetic and importantly controlled substances under the Federal Controlled Substances Act," he said. HEAVY DRINKING SURGES AMONG AMERICANS IN ONE AGE GROUP AS OTHER GENERATIONS CUT BACK "Those products never should have been on the market in the first place in those locations." The Mississippi Kratom Consumer Protection Act (KCPA) is a state law that regulates the sale of kratom rather than banning it. The law establishes standards for who may sell kratom, which products are permitted and how they must be labeled, while prohibiting certain adulterated or high-potency products. "Why were they not enforcing it?" Haddow questioned. Natural vs. synthetic According to Haddow, natural kratom leaves have been used for centuries in Southeast Asia. He argued there have been no published reports of deaths linked to traditional leaf use in the region, although medical literature does describe some adverse effects associated with long-term use. Haddow said he believes kratom first spread in the U.S. after the Vietnam War, when returning soldiers and Southeast Asian immigrants brought it back from the region. However, researchers note that this origin story remains unsubstantiated in the published literature. "We need to regulate them, and as we represent consumers, we're going to fight for that." "And then these amateur chemists got involved and started tinkering with the alkaloids in the natural plant and started to adulterate them, and that appropriately got kratom on the radar of both the DEA and the FDA," he said. In 2012, the FDA issued an import alert on kratom products, and the DEA sought to temporarily classify kratom's primary alkaloids as Schedule I substances in 2016 before withdrawing the proposal following public comment. More recently, the agencies have raised concerns about concentrated and chemically modified kratom products, including those containing high levels of 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH). "What these bad actors have done is completely alter the composition of the natural kratom plant," Haddow said. "They rearranged the molecules. They've chemically synthesized them with high-concentration chlorine and baking soda and other nefarious production methods so that they deliver what is in fact a signature opioid to consumers in the United States." Calls for stronger enforcement The association’s focus now is on banning synthetic products and protecting the natural leaf, Haddow said. "It is improper for any government agency across the country to be blaming natural leaf kratom for any adverse event that is properly attributable to a synthetic opioid," he added, expressing his viewpoint. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "If we were to take coffee and extract caffeine from it and then highly concentrate it to a level in which it is fatal and someone ingested it and died, we wouldn't blame coffee. We would blame the bad actor that took and extracted that caffeine, because caffeine is in its natural form and coffee is not dangerous. The same is true for natural kratom." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Haddow said 7-OH products — including pseudoindoxyl and compounds known as MGM-15 and MGM-16 — should not be considered kratom. "[They] are synthetic opioids, all of which should be enforced by both the federal and local law enforcement agencies," he said. "We advocate strongly for proper clarification of these dangerous products as opposed to natural kratom, which is literally helping people with their health and wellness and saving lives." Haddow cited an NIH-led study that is moving forward to evaluate whether purified mitragynine, the main alkaloid in the kratom plant, could help treat opioid use disorder. Regulation over prohibition Haddow said the association supports state regulations that require testing, labeling and age restrictions rather than outright bans. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Make sure the product formulations are safe, make sure the products are labeled correctly and make sure they're age-restricted," he urged. "Twenty-one and up should be the only people who have access to these products. "We need to regulate them, and as we represent consumers, we're going to fight for that." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The FDA maintains that kratom has not been approved for any medical use and has warned of some risks, including dependence, contamination and adverse events, while researchers continue to study both the plant and its individual compounds.

Captação de coração, rins e tecidos no HPM mobilizou transporte aéreo e equipes especializadas — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Uma história de solidariedade e amor ao próximo emocionou a rede de saúde de Macaé. O servidor público Lucas Nunes Hardie, de 40 anos, tornou-se doador múltiplo de órgãos e tecidos após passar por um grave acidente de trânsito. O procedimento de captação, realizado no Hospital Público Municipal (HPM), incluiu a doação de coração, fígado, rins, pâncreas, córneas e ossos, salvando e transformando a vida de pacientes que aguardavam na fila de transplantes.

A decisão de autorizar o procedimento partiu da irmã de Lucas, Lidiane Nunes, respeitando o desejo manifestado em vida pelo profissional de saúde. Para superar o momento de dor e vencer o tabu familiar, o apoio humanizado oferecido pelas equipes médicas foi fundamental.

O coração do doador, órgão de alta complexidade e raridade para compatibilidade, foi transportado de helicóptero diretamente do HPM no mesmo dia.

Município realiza congresso de conscientização na Câmara para incentivar a conversa em família — Foto: Arquivo Secom

O gesto de generosidade reflete o trabalho contínuo de conscientização desenvolvido na cidade. Macaé registra uma taxa de aceite familiar para doação de órgãos de 55,5%, índice muito superior à média do estado do Rio de Janeiro, que é de 33%. O trabalho de suporte e acolhimento prestado pela Equipe Hospitalar de Doação de Órgãos e Tecidos (e-DOT) no momento do luto é apontado como o grande diferencial para garantir o respeito à vontade dos doadores.

Para debater a importância do tema e engajar a sociedade, a prefeitura promove o Congresso Municipal de Conscientização na Câmara de Vereadores, abordando a doação como um ato de transformação e preservação de vidas. O evento gratuito e aberto ao público incentiva que moradores conversem com seus parentes em casa sobre o desejo de se tornarem doadores.

articles.title: Lito Sousa: vídeo mostra influencer em pegadinha do Faustão | G1
articles.standfirst: Influencer de aviação, que morreu aos 59 anos, participou de brincadeira do Domingão do Faustão por volta dos anos 2000 e relembrou o episódio nas redes sociais em 2025.
articles.summary: Lito Sousa, criador do canal Aviões e Músicas que morreu aos 59 anos, relembrou participação em pegadinha do Faustão gravada nos anos 2000.
articles.body:
Lito Sousa relembrou participação em pegadinha do Faustão nas redes sociais em 2025. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/@lito

O influenciador Lito Sousa, que morreu nesta quinta-feira (1º), aos 59 anos, em São Paulo , participou de uma pegadinha do Domingão do Faustão por volta dos anos 2000, antes de se tornar conhecido na internet.

Décadas depois, o próprio criador de conteúdo relembrou o episódio nas redes sociais e brincou com o fato de ter caído na pegadinha.

No vídeo, o apresentador Fausto Silva convida a dupla sertaneja Gian & Giovani a escolher uma das brincadeiras exibidas pelo programa. Os cantores optam pela do banco que se mexe, instalado em uma rua para surpreender quem se sentasse nele.

Lito aparece entre as pessoas que caíram na "armadilha" preparada pela produção do programa.

Em abril de 2022, ele publicou o vídeo da pegadinha em seu canal no YouTube, o Aviões e Músicas, conhecido por conteúdos sobre aviação. A gravação ultrapassou 150 mil visualizações.

Em dezembro de 2025, o influenciador voltou a compartilhar o registro no Instagram e no Facebook. Na ocasião, brincou com a própria participação na atração. "Pra descontrair nessa segundona de manhã, sabia que eu já caí numa pegadinha do Faustão?", escreveu.

Joselito Geraldo de Sousa, conhecido como Lito Sousa, era um dos principais influenciadores brasileiros especializados em aviação. Mecânico de aeronaves com mais de 36 anos de experiência no setor, trabalhou em empresas como Varig, Transbrasil e United Airlines.

Ficou conhecido pelo canal Aviões e Músicas, no YouTube, onde explicava temas como segurança aérea, turbulências e acidentes em linguagem acessível. O canal reúne mais de 3,5 milhões de inscritos.

Lito Sousa, influenciador e especialista em aviação que sofria com doença rara, morre em São Paulo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Em 2026, Lito passou a compartilhar com os seguidores informações sobre problemas de saúde. Após revelar um diagnóstico de câncer de próstata, ele recebeu, em agosto, o diagnóstico de doença de Creutzfeldt-Jakob, uma condição neurodegenerativa rara e progressiva.

Segundo estudo do Ministério da Saúde, a doença teve 547 casos confirmados no Brasil entre 2005 e 2021.

Familiares e o Hospital Albert Einstein, onde Lito estava internado, confirmaram a morte do influenciador na noite desta quinta. Em um post no Instagram, a esposa Mila Seidl escreveu: "Um grande abraço e até o próximo voo. Foi uma honra ter viajado com você. Te amo. Sempre". Ele deixa um filho de 7 anos.

O corpo de Lito será velado nesta sexta-feira (2) na Zona Norte da capital paulista. Haverá um espaço aberto ao público, das 9h às 12h, na Avenida Braz Leme, 2.594. Familiares e amigos próximos poderão se despedir em um local reservado.

No hospital, Lito Sousa comemora 4 milhões de seguidores em seu canal — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

articles.title: Hospital São José amplia atuação em ortopedia com chegada de tecnologia robótica | G1
articles.standfirst: Plataforma CORI passa a integrar estrutura do hospital e permite procedimentos mais personalizados, com planejamento individualizado para cada paciente
articles.summary: Plataforma CORI passa a integrar estrutura do hospital e permite procedimentos mais personalizados, com planejamento individualizado para cada paciente
articles.body:
A cirurgia robótica na ortopedia passa a fazer parte da realidade do Hospital São José, em Criciúma. A instituição recebeu a plataforma CORI, tecnologia desenvolvida pela Smith+Nephew, que será utilizada inicialmente em procedimentos de artroplastia do joelho e, futuramente, também poderá ser aplicada em cirurgias de artroplastia do quadril. A implantação envolve o Hospital São José, a equipe da Levve Ortopedia e a Smith+Nephew.

A chegada da tecnologia representa um novo avanço na estrutura de atendimento em ortopedia do HSJosé, ampliando os recursos disponíveis para o planejamento e a realização de procedimentos. A plataforma permite que o planejamento cirúrgico seja realizado de forma individualizada, considerando as características anatômicas de cada paciente.

“Estamos trazendo tecnologia de ponta que oferece ainda mais precisão e segurança aos procedimentos e coloca o nosso hospital em um novo patamar de inovação. É tecnologia a serviço da medicina, dos nossos profissionais e, principalmente, dos nossos pacientes. Mais um grande avanço para o Hospital São José e também para toda a nossa região”, destaca o diretor administrativo do Hospital São José, Cristiano Lazzarin.

O ortopedista do HSJosé e da Levve Ortopedia, Dr. Mario César Búrigo, explica que a implantação da plataforma é resultado de um trabalho conjunto entre as instituições envolvidas.

“Esse é um projeto conjunto entre a Smith+Nephew, o Hospital São José e a Levve Ortopedia. Estamos iniciando a capacitação da equipe de cirurgiões para utilização da plataforma CORI, que traz uma nova possibilidade para os procedimentos de cirurgia robótica dentro da ortopedia”, afirma.

Também ortopedista do HSJosé e da Levve Ortopedia, Dr. Ericsson Reinaldo Pires ressalta que a tecnologia chega com o objetivo de ampliar a precisão dos procedimentos e qualificar ainda mais a assistência oferecida aos pacientes.

“Estamos fazendo o treinamento da tecnologia robótica do sistema CORI, que vai trazer mais precisão, qualidade e conforto para os nossos pacientes. Nós, da equipe Levve, junto com o Hospital São José, estamos buscando o melhor para cada paciente, porque, para nós, cada vida importa”, afirma.

Robô da ortopedia no Hospital São José — Foto: Divulgação/Hospital São José

Entre os principais diferenciais da plataforma está a possibilidade de realizar um planejamento cirúrgico personalizado. Segundo o ortopedista Dr. Fernando Lupselo, a tecnologia permite considerar as particularidades de cada paciente na definição da estratégia do procedimento.

“As vantagens que essa tecnologia traz para a cirurgia de artroplastia do joelho e, no futuro, para a cirurgia de artroplastia do quadril, são as cirurgias personalizadas. O planejamento é feito em cima do caso do paciente, encontrando os melhores posicionamentos que garantam a melhor performance biomecânica para aquela articulação”, explica.

Para o especialista, a incorporação da tecnologia representa a integração entre os avanços tecnológicos e a evolução da própria prática médica. “Isso é cirurgia moderna, tecnologia aliada a melhores resultados e longevidade dos pacientes”, completa.

A plataforma CORI utiliza recursos de planejamento e assistência robótica para auxiliar o cirurgião durante o procedimento. A tecnologia não substitui a atuação médica, mas oferece informações e ferramentas que contribuem para a tomada de decisão e para a execução de um procedimento planejado de acordo com as características de cada paciente.

Descubra como a inovação está revolucionando os tratamentos ortopédicos. Acesse o site do Hospital São José e conheça todos os diferenciais da instituição.

articles.title: Pai é preso após agredir a própria filha com cabo de vassoura | G1
articles.standfirst: Menina chegou com hematomas na escola e Guarda Municipal foi acionada. Pai admitiu as agressões e foi preso em flagrante.
articles.summary: Menina chegou com hematomas na escola e Guarda Municipal foi acionada. Pai admitiu as agressões e foi preso em flagrante.
articles.body:
Delegacia Regional de Vila Velha, Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Gazeta

Um homem de 27 anos foi preso depois de agredir a própria filha de 11 anos anos com um cabo de vassoura, em Vila Velha , na Grande Vitória, na tarde desta quinta-feira (1°). O caso foi descoberto quando a menina chegou à escola com hematomas e ferimentos visíveis no rosto e nos braços.

Os nomes dos envolvidos e o bairro da residência da vítima não estão sendo divulgados para preservar a identidade da criança, conforme prevê o Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente (Ecriad).

Segundo informações da Guarda Municipal, a aluna da rede municipal relatou que estava sentindo dores e os machucados foram constatados por uma pedagoga. A mãe foi acionada e compareceu à escola.

O pai da criança também foi ao local. Questionado sobre o ocorrido, ele confirmou a agressão e relatou que o fato aconteceu durante uma situação de conflito familiar, afirmando ter “perdido a cabeça” depois de encontrar a filha em casa com um rapaz.

A menina foi encaminhada para um Pronto Atendimento (PA) do município e depois transferida para o Hospital Estadual Infantil Nossa Senhora da Glória (HINSG), em Vitória. Não foram divulgadas informações sobre o estado de saúde.

O Conselho Tutelar também foi acionado para acompanhar a ocorrência, mas apenas orientou que o caso fosse entregue na delegacia, e nenhum conselheiro compareceu. Segundo a polícia, existe um histórico de abusos sofridos pela menina.

O pai foi preso em flagrante e encaminhado para a Delegacia Regional de Vila Velha. O homem foi autuado por maus-tratos contra menor de idade e vai ser encaminhado para um presídio na manhã desta sexta-feira (2).

articles.title: Homem morre após ser baleado em rua na Zona Leste de Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: A vítima foi transferida para o Hospital de Urgência de Teresina (HUT). No entanto, morreu durante o deslocamento para a unidade de saúde.
articles.summary: A vítima foi transferida para o Hospital de Urgência de Teresina (HUT). No entanto, morreu durante o deslocamento para a unidade de saúde.
articles.body:
Victor Hugo Gomes do Nascimento morreu após ser baleado na noite de quinta-feira (1º), na Rua Nossa Senhora dos Remédios, no bairro Verde Lar, Zona Leste de Teresina . Segundo o 29º Batalhão da Polícia Militar (29º BPM), a vítima chegou a ser socorrida, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

De acordo com a Polícia Militar, moradores acionaram a equipe após ouvirem disparos por volta das 21h40. Quando os policiais chegaram ao local, foram informados de que o rapaz já havia sido levado para a Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) do Satélite.

Em seguida, ele foi transferido para o Hospital de Urgência de Teresina (HUT). No entanto, morreu durante o deslocamento para a unidade de saúde.

Testemunhas informaram aos policiais que dois homens em uma motocicleta se aproximaram da vítima e efetuaram vários disparos. Os suspeitos vestiam roupas pretas, e um deles carregava uma bolsa semelhante à utilizada por entregadores de aplicativo.

Após o crime, a dupla fugiu e não havia sido localizada até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A perícia criminal foi acionada e recolheu dois cartuchos de arma de fogo no local. O material será submetido à análise.

O Departamento de Homicídio e Proteção à Pessoa (DHPP) vai investigar a motivação do crime e deve identificar os responsáveis.

Outro homem foi morto no bairro na noite anterior

Um homem chamado João Manoel da Silva foi assassinado a tiros na noite de quarta-feira (30), na região do bairro Verde Lar. João é suspeito de ter participado de um assalto a uma sorveteria na região horas antes de ser morto, segundo a Polícia Militar do Piauí (PM-PI).

Segundo o 29º BPM, policiais foram chamados para a Rua São Francisco por volta das 22h30. Ao chegarem ao local, encontraram a vítima morta no chão, com marcas que pareciam ser de arma de fogo.

As circunstâncias do crime ainda são investigadas. Nenhum responsável foi localizado.

articles.title: Bebê engasga e é salva por policial em centro de triagem de presos | G1
articles.standfirst: Criança de 1 ano e 9 meses chegou sem ar e roxa a uma instituição da polícia penal, mas foi salva após manobra de agente.
articles.summary: Criança de 1 ano e 9 meses chegou sem ar e roxa a uma instituição da polícia penal, mas foi salva após manobra de agente.
articles.body:
Uma bebê de 1 ano e 9 meses foi salva de engasgamento por um policial civil na noite de segunda-feira (28), em Porto Alegre . A criança chegou sem ar e com a coloração roxa.

Segundo a mãe, Gabriela Silva, Sophia comia uma bolacha de água e sal quando se engasgou . Ao perceber que a filha não conseguia respirar, ela tentou realizar manobras e, em seguida, pediu ajuda a um vizinho que tinha carro para levá-las em busca de socorro.

O policial civil Matheus Leonardo Figueiredo estava a serviço no Núcleo de Gestão Estratégica de Sistema Prisional (Nugesp) quando um carro chegou em velocidade ao local. Gabriela desceu do veículo com a filha nos braços e passou a gritar por ajuda .

"Ela gritava: minha filha está morrendo. Consegui sair pelo portão, coloquei o joelho no diafragma dela e comecei a fazer manobras na coluna. Demorou muito, cerca de 3 minutos. Eu também fazia sucção na boca para tentar desobstruir Ela estava bastante roxa, mas aos poucos o corpo começou a ganhar rigidez e ela voltou à coloração normal", relata o agente.

De acordo com a mãe, o momento foi um sufoco . Gabriela estima que toda a ação, desde o engasgamento, tenha durado cerca de 3 minutos.

"Um momento de terror", resume Gabriela. "Ela já estava mole, praticamente desmaiada. Foi muito horrível", diz.

Sophia voltou a respirar e, em seguida, foi encaminhada ao Hospital de Pronto Socorro (HPS) da capital gaúcha. Ela foi atendida e passa bem .

“Uma sensação que não há nada na polícia que possa me dar igual a isso. Uma sensação de alívio, de alegria de fazer algo que não sei se vou ter oportunidade de fazer de novo. Espero que não precise novamente”, relata o policial.

O policial civil Matheus Leonardo Figueiredo e a bebê Sophia, que ajudou a salvar de engasgo — Foto: Imagem cedida

O agente conta que recebeu as instruções em um curso realizado pelo soldado Souza Neves, da Brigada Militar, sendo ele um policial civil, e que o fato ocorreu em uma sede da polícia penal.
